ModuleOwner.schema:
<Property>
            <Name>ModuleOwner</Name>
            <HasImplementation>1</HasImplementation>
            <ValueDefinition>
              <DataType>Array</DataType>
              <Name>ModuleLimits</Name>
              <Description>Maximum allowed amount of building modules (set to 0 for unlimited modules)</Description>
              <DataSet>ModuleType</DataSet>
              <Items>
                <ValueDefinition>
                  <DataType>Integer</DataType>
                  <Name>Limit</Name>
                </ValueDefinition>
              </Items>
            </ValueDefinition>
            <ValueDefinition>
              <DataType>Integer</DataType>
              <Name>ModulesRequiredForFullProductivity</Name>
              <Description>if set to 0, all (ModuleLimit) modules are neded</Description>
              <Min>0</Min>
            </ValueDefinition>
            <ValueDefinition>
              <DataType>Vector</DataType>
              <Name>ConstructionOptions</Name>
              <Items>
                <ValueDefinition>
                  <DataType>Asset</DataType>
                  <Name>ModuleGUID</Name>
                  <NeededProperty>BuildingModule</NeededProperty>
                </ValueDefinition>
              </Items>
            </ValueDefinition>
            <ValueDefinition>
              <DataType>Asset</DataType>
              <Name>AdditionalModule</Name>
              <Description>Extra module that can be applied to this module owner. (i.e. Bright Harvest Tractor)</Description>
            </ValueDefinition>
            <ValueDefinition>
              <DataType>Boolean</DataType>
              <Name>AdditionalModuleMustBeMainBuildingAdjacent</Name>
              <Description>e.g. Tractor / Silo module with special build rules different to other modules</Description>
            </ValueDefinition>
            <ValueDefinition>
              <DataType>Boolean</DataType>
              <Name>AdjustModuleOrientationOnceSpecialModuleWasPlaced</Name>
              <Description>If the main modules should be axis oriented if a tractor / silo / fertilizer module was added. Used for vehicle feedback on farms</Description>
            </ValueDefinition>
            <ValueDefinition>
              <DataType>Struct</DataType>
              <Name>FertilizerModuleData</Name>
              <Items>
                <ValueDefinition>
                  <DataType>Asset</DataType>
                  <Name>Module</Name>
                  <NeededProperty>BuildingModule</NeededProperty>
                </ValueDefinition>
                <ValueDefinition>
                  <DataType>Boolean</DataType>
                  <Name>MustBeMainBuildingAdjacent</Name>
                </ValueDefinition>
              </Items>
            </ValueDefinition>
            <ValueDefinition>
              <DataType>Integer</DataType>
              <Name>ModuleBuildRadius</Name>
              <Description>set to 0 if modules have to be build adjacent</Description>
            </ValueDefinition>
            <ValueDefinition>
              <DataType>Boolean</DataType>
              <Name>AllowModulesInSameHarbor</Name>
              <Description>Modules can be build free like with ModuleBuildRadius, but the build area is defined by the coastline</Description>
            </ValueDefinition>
            <ValueDefinition>
              <DataType>Integer</DataType>
              <Name>ImplicitProductivityModules</Name>
              <Description>for productivity calculkation of farms, the main building counts as x additional farmfields</Description>
            </ValueDefinition>
            <ValueDefinition>
              <DataType>Integer</DataType>
              <Name>AddModuleLimit</Name>
              <Description>Holding shift while building modules increases the module limit for ModuleType_Main</Description>
              <Min>0</Min>
              <Max>100</Max>
            </ValueDefinition>
            <ValueDefinition>
              <DataType>Integer</DataType>
              <Name>HardFarmsConfig</Name>
            </ValueDefinition>
            <ValueDefinition>
              <DataType>Boolean</DataType>
              <Name>EnableIrrigationFertilizer</Name>
            </ValueDefinition>
            <ValueDefinition>
              <DataType>Flags</DataType>
              <Name>IrrigationLevelsWorking</Name>
              <DataSet>IrrigationLevel</DataSet>
            </ValueDefinition>
            <ValueDefinition>
              <DataType>Flags</DataType>
              <Name>IrrigationLevelsBoosting</Name>
              <DataSet>IrrigationLevel</DataSet>
            </ValueDefinition>
            <ValueDefinition>
              <DataType>Boolean</DataType>
              <Name>DestroyModulesDuringMoveAllowed</Name>
            </ValueDefinition>
            <ValueDefinition>
              <DataType>Float</DataType>
              <Name>MaxProductivityBoostForBoostedModules</Name>
            </ValueDefinition>
            <ValueDefinition>
              <DataType>Choice</DataType>
              <Name>FarmType</Name>
              <DataSet>FarmType</DataSet>
            </ValueDefinition>
            <ValueDefinition>
              <DataType>Integer</DataType>
              <Name>AmountNonIrrigatedModulesRequiredForInfolayer</Name>
            </ValueDefinition>
            <ValueDefinition>
              <DataType>Asset</DataType>
              <Name>MissingIrrigationInfolayerIcon</Name>
              <NeededProperty>InfoLayerIcon</NeededProperty>
            </ValueDefinition>
            <ValueDefinition>
              <DataType>Boolean</DataType>
              <Name>UseSingleModuleUpgrading</Name>
              <Description>If this is set then only the selected module will be upgraded after clicking on the upgrade from blueprint button. Otherwise all will be upgraded at once (farm fields for example)</Description>
            </ValueDefinition>
            <ValueDefinition>
              <DataType>Struct</DataType>
              <Name>BlueprintModuleOption</Name>
              <Items>
                <ValueDefinition>
                  <DataType>Asset</DataType>
                  <Name>ModuleButtonIcon</Name>
                  <Description>owners with multiple construction options should configure the module button for the blueprint menu. If not configured, the first construction option is used (default for farms)</Description>
                </ValueDefinition>
                <ValueDefinition>
                  <DataType>Text</DataType>
                  <Name>ModulePopupDescription</Name>
                </ValueDefinition>
                <ValueDefinition>
                  <DataType>Text</DataType>
                  <Name>ModulePopupHeader</Name>
                </ValueDefinition>
                <ValueDefinition>
                  <DataType>Asset</DataType>
                  <Name>ModuleButtonInfotip</Name>
                  <NeededProperty>Infotip</NeededProperty>
                </ValueDefinition>
                <ValueDefinition>
                  <DataType>Boolean</DataType>
                  <Name>ShowRemainingModuleCount</Name>

              </Items>
              <Description>for the blueprint menu: how should the module button look like and is there a popup with multiple options?</Description>
            </ValueDefinition>
          </Property>

Object.schema:
<Property>
        <Name>Object</Name>
        <ValueDefinition>
          <DataType>Choice</DataType>
          <Name>Type</Name>
          <DataSet>ObjectType</DataSet>
        </ValueDefinition>
        <ValueDefinition>
          <DataType>Vector</DataType>
          <Name>Variations</Name>
          <Description>Vector of variations. </Description>
          <Items>
            <ValueDefinition>
              <DataType>FileName</DataType>
              <Name>Filename</Name>

              <Filter>Config or Prop|*.cfg;*.prp</Filter>
            </ValueDefinition>
          </Items>
        </ValueDefinition>
        <ValueDefinition>
          <DataType>Struct</DataType>
          <Name>Skins</Name>
          <Items>
            <ValueDefinition>
              <DataType>Text</DataType>
              <Name>DefaultSkinName</Name>
              <Description>Name of the Default skin in the infotip</Description>
              <NeededProperty>Text</NeededProperty>
            </ValueDefinition>
            <ValueDefinition>
              <DataType>Text</DataType>
              <Name>DefaultSkinDescription</Name>
              <Description>Fluff text of the default skin in the infotip</Description>
              <NeededProperty>Text</NeededProperty>
            </ValueDefinition>
            <ValueDefinition>
              <DataType>Text</DataType>
              <Name>DefaultSkinCategoryName</Name>
              <NeededProperty>Text</NeededProperty>
              <Description>Description of the category a skin belongs to. Like name of a CDLC</Description>
            </ValueDefinition>
            <ValueDefinition>
              <DataType>FileName</DataType>
              <Name>OverrideDefaultIcon</Name>
              <Description>Optional Parameter: If this path is set it overrides the standard icon for the Default Skin</Description>
            </ValueDefinition>
            <ValueDefinition>
              <DataType>Vector</DataType>
              <Name>SkinList</Name>
              <Description>List of skin assets</Description>
              <Items>
                <ValueDefinition>
                  <DataType>Asset</DataType>
                  <Name>SkinAssetGuid</Name>
                  <NeededProperty>Skin</NeededProperty>
                </ValueDefinition>
              </Items>
            </ValueDefinition>
          </Items>
        </ValueDefinition>
        <ValueDefinition>
          <DataType>Boolean</DataType>
          <Name>AssignDefaultParticipant</Name>
          <Description>True = When the object is placed in the editor. The assigned participant will be based on this asset configuration, not on the current editor state.</Description>
        </ValueDefinition>
        <ValueDefinition>
          <DataType>Choice</DataType>
          <Name>DefaultParticipant</Name>
          <Description>The role of a participant that is assigned to this object by default when placed in the editor.</Description>
          <DataSet>ParticipantID</DataSet>
        </ValueDefinition>
        <ValueDefinition>
          <DataType>Boolean</DataType>
          <Name>AddToObjectGroups</Name>

        </ValueDefinition>
        <ValueDefinition>
          <DataType>Boolean</DataType>
          <Name>AddToEditorObjectGrid</Name>
        </ValueDefinition>
        <ValueDefinition>
          <DataType>Boolean</DataType>
          <Name>PlacableInEditor</Name>
        </ValueDefinition>
        <ValueDefinition>
          <DataType>Boolean</DataType>
          <Name>SelectableInEditor</Name>
        </ValueDefinition>
        <ValueDefinition>
          <DataType>Boolean</DataType>
          <Name>IgnoreForMinimapGeneration</Name>

        </ValueDefinition>
        <ValueDefinition>
          <DataType>Boolean</DataType>
          <Name>LoadFromDemoSavegame</Name>
        </ValueDefinition>
        <ValueDefinition>
          <DataType>Boolean</DataType>
          <Name>LoadFromDemoMap</Name>
        </ValueDefinition>
      </Property>

ObjectFilter.schema:
<Property>
            <Name>ObjectFilter</Name>
            <ValueDefinition>
              <DataType>String</DataType>
              <Name>ObjectLabel</Name>
              <Description>object label of a single object or group label for a group of objects</Description>

ParticipantMessages.schema:
<Property>
            <Name>ParticipantMessages</Name>
            <Description>How does the Participant react to certain Triggers? </Description>
            <ValueDefinition>
              <DataType>Array</DataType>
              <Name>MessageTriggers</Name>
              <DataSet>ParticipantMessageTrigger</DataSet>
              <Items>
                <ValueDefinition>
                  <DataType>Vector</DataType>
                  <Name>Reactions</Name>
                  <Description>The conditions for all Reactions will be checked from top to bottom. As soon as one is Fulfilled, The Reaction is triggered and the evaluation is stopped.</Description>
                  <Items>
                    <ValueDefinition>
                      <DataType>Flags</DataType>
                      <Name>DisabledForGameType</Name>
                      <DataSet>GameType</DataSet>
                    </ValueDefinition>
                    <ValueDefinition>
                      <DataType>Choice</DataType>
                      <Name>MyRole</Name>
                      <DataSet>ParticipantMessageRole</DataSet>
                    </ValueDefinition>
                    <ValueDefinition>
                      <DataType>Flags</DataType>
                      <Name>RequiredDiplomacyState</Name>
                      <Description>Reaction is only executed when the two related participants have one of the required diplomacyStates. Empty = Dont Care. (All Checked = Dont Care, but Empty is Recommended)</Description>
                      <DataSet>DiplomacyState</DataSet>
                    </ValueDefinition>
                    <ValueDefinition>
                      <DataType>Choice</DataType>
                      <Name>RequiredReputationState</Name>
                      <DataSet>ParticipantMessageReputation</DataSet>
                    </ValueDefinition>
                    <ValueDefinition>
                      <DataType>Choice</DataType>
                      <Name>RequiredReputationParticipant</Name>
                      <DataSet>ParticipantID</DataSet>
                      <AllowEmpty>1</AllowEmpty>
                    </ValueDefinition>
                    <ValueDefinition>
                      <DataType>Integer</DataType>
                      <Name>RequiredReputation</Name>
                    </ValueDefinition>
                    <ValueDefinition>
                      <DataType>Asset</DataType>
                      <Name>RequiredContextAsset</Name>
                      <Description>Type of asset depends on trigger (e.g. a buildingAsset for CREATE_CULTURAL_BUILDING).  If a message has an asset as precondition, it will only be executed if the trigger relates to the same asset</Description>
                    </ValueDefinition>
                    <ValueDefinition>
                      <DataType>Flags</DataType>
                      <Name>RequiredContextMenu</Name>
                      <Description>Reaction is only executed when the given menu is currently opened</Description>
                      <DataSet>GUIState</DataSet>
                    </ValueDefinition>
                    <ValueDefinition>
                      <DataType>Integer</DataType>
                      <Name>RequiredContextValueThreshold</Name>
                      <Description>-1 = Ignore this Requirement. Some Triggers are Fired with a ContextValue (e.g. "Propaganda" can be slight(0), medium(1), heavy(2), ...). If you set this value to X, than the reaction is triggered for all values <= X.</Description>
                      <Min>-1</Min>
                    </ValueDefinition>
                    <ValueDefinition>
                      <DataType>Float</DataType>
                      <Name>Probability</Name>
                      <Description>If this trigger occurs, how likely (0.0 = never, 1.0 = always) will the reaction be executed?</Description>
                      <Min>0</Min>
                      <Max>1</Max>
                    </ValueDefinition>
                    <ValueDefinition>
                      <DataType>Boolean</DataType>
                      <Name>ProbabilityIsOneForFirstOccurence</Name>
                      <Description>Only Relevant when Probability != 1. Forces the Probability of a Reaction to 100% for first occurence of this trigger.</Description>
                    </ValueDefinition>
                    <ValueDefinition>
                      <DataType>Integer</DataType>
                      <Name>IgnoreFirstOccurences</Name>
                      <Description>How many Triggers should be ignored before the first Reaction is Executed? 0 = Execute on first Trigger Occurence</Description>
                      <Min>0</Min>
                      <Max>255</Max>
                    </ValueDefinition>
                    <ValueDefinition>
                      <DataType>Integer</DataType>
                      <Name>CooldownOccurences</Name>
                      <Description>After an Execution of this Reaction, how many Triggers are ignored before the next Reaction is Executed? 0 = Execute on every consecutive Trigger Occurence.</Description>
                      <Min>0</Min>
                      <Max>255</Max>
                    </ValueDefinition>
                    <ValueDefinition>
                      <DataType>Time</DataType>
                      <Name>CooldownTime</Name>
                      <Description>After an Execution of this Reaction, how much time has to pass before this Reaction is allowed to be Executed again?</Description>
                    </ValueDefinition>
                    <ValueDefinition>
                      <DataType>Choice</DataType>
                      <Name>SideEffect</Name>
                      <Description>Should the Reaction Execute Any Side Effects? (Details for the Side Effect can be configured in EffectValue). Note: Reputation Changes always Change What THIS profile thinks of the other one (human / other).</Description>
                      <DataSet>ParticipantMessageEffect</DataSet>
                    </ValueDefinition>
                    <ValueDefinition>
                      <DataType>Integer</DataType>
                      <Name>SideEffectValue</Name>
                      <Description>If SideEffect needs a value as additional context, put it in here</Description>
                      <Min>-1000</Min>
                      <Max>1000</Max>
                    </ValueDefinition>
                    <ValueDefinition>
                      <DataType>Asset</DataType>
                      <Name>NotificationGUID</Name>
                      <Description>Notification that is executed by this Reaction</Description>
                    </ValueDefinition>
                    <ValueDefinition>
                      <DataType>AutoCreateAsset</DataType>
                      <Name>Notification</Name>
                      <Description>Notification that is executed by this Reaction (if NotificationGUID is not set)</Description>
                      <AllowedTemplates>CharacterNotification;SideNotification</AllowedTemplates>
                      <AllowedProperties/>
                    </ValueDefinition>
                    <ValueDefinition>
                      <DataType>Asset</DataType>
                      <Name>ReputationLogEntry</Name>
                      <NeededProperty>Text</NeededProperty>
                    </ValueDefinition>
                    <ValueDefinition>
                      <DataType>Vector</DataType>
                      <Name>UnlockAssets</Name>
                      <Items>
                        <ValueDefinition>
                          <DataType>Asset</DataType>
                          <Name>UnlockAsset</Name>
                        </ValueDefinition>
                      </Items>
                    </ValueDefinition>
                    <ValueDefinition>
                      <DataType>Flags</DataType>
                      <Name>NotificationFilter</Name>
                      <DataSet>ParticipantMessageFilter</DataSet>
                    </ValueDefinition>
                  </Items>
                </ValueDefinition>
              </Items>
            </ValueDefinition>
          </Property>

        </ValueDefinition>

          <IsProValue>1</IsProValue>
          <AllowedTemplates>Actions</AllowedTemplates>
          <AllowedProperties/>
        </ValueDefinition>
        <ValueDefinition>

          <Category>Action Trigger</Category>
          <IsProValue>1</IsProValue>
          <AllowedTemplates>Actions</AllowedTemplates>
          <AllowedProperties/>
        </ValueDefinition>
        <ValueDefinition>
          <DataType>AutoCreateAsset</DataType>

          <IsProValue>1</IsProValue>

          <AllowedProperties/>

          <AllowedProperties/>
        </ValueDefinition>

          <AllowedProperties/>

          <AllowedTemplates>Actions</AllowedTemplates>
          <AllowedProperties/>

          <IsProValue>1</IsProValue>
          <AllowedTemplates>Actions</AllowedTemplates>
          <AllowedProperties/>
        </ValueDefinition>

          <Category>Action Trigger</Category>
          <IsProValue>1</IsProValue>
          <AllowedTemplates>Actions</AllowedTemplates>
          <AllowedProperties/>

          <DataType>Integer</DataType>
          <Name>MaxSolveCount</Name>
          <Description>Maximum number that this quest can be solved. <= 0 means infinite calls are possible</Description>
        </ValueDefinition>
        <ValueDefinition>
          <DataType>Integer</DataType>
          <Name>MaxAbortCount</Name>
          <Description>Maximum number that this quest can be aborted. <= 0 means infinite calls are possible</Description>

          <DataType>Boolean</DataType>

        <ValueDefinition>
          <DataType>Time</DataType>

          <IsProValue>1</IsProValue>
        </ValueDefinition>

          <DataType>Time</DataType>

          <IsProValue>1</IsProValue>
        </ValueDefinition>

          <DataType>Choice</DataType>

          <IsProValue>1</IsProValue>
          <DataSet>QuestCategory</DataSet>
        </ValueDefinition>

          <IsProValue>1</IsProValue>

          <DataType>Flags</DataType>

          <Category>PreConditions</Category>
          <DataSet>ProgressLevel</DataSet>
        </ValueDefinition>
        <ValueDefinition>
          <DataType>Time</DataType>
          <Name>LatencyTimer</Name>
          <Description>Latency before a quest can start after all other preconditions are fulfilled. The latency starts again if a single precondition check fails during the countdown. This needs to be checked over the whole duration and is EXPENSIVE for game performance</Description>
          <Category>PreConditions</Category>
        </ValueDefinition>
        <ValueDefinition>
          <DataType>Time</DataType>
          <Name>DelayTimer</Name>
          <Description>Delay the quest after the preconditions were fulfilled once. The preconditions will be checked once again after the delay finished. This is a CHEAPER alternative to the latency timer in terms of performance</Description>
          <Category>PreConditions</Category>
        </ValueDefinition>
        <ValueDefinition>
          <DataType>Choice</DataType>
          <Name>QuestTrackerVisibility</Name>
          <Description>Defines when this quest will be visible in the quest tracker.</Description>
          <Category>Quest Category</Category>
          <DataSet>QuestTrackerVisibility</DataSet>

        <ValueDefinition>
          <DataType>Choice</DataType>

          <AllowedProperties/>

          <Category>PreConditions</Category>
        </ValueDefinition>

            <ValueDefinition>
              <DataType>Asset</DataType>
              <Name>SessionOrRegion</Name>
              <Description>Session or region(= list of sessions) allowed here</Description>
              <NeededProperty>Session;Region</NeededProperty>
            </ValueDefinition>
          </Items>
        </ValueDefinition>
        <ValueDefinition>
          <DataType>Vector</DataType>
          <Name>QuestBlockedSessions</Name>
          <Description>If not empty, the quest can not be triggered in one of the specified sessions</Description>
          <Category>PreConditions</Category>
          <Items>
            <ValueDefinition>
              <DataType>Asset</DataType>
              <Name>SessionOrRegion</Name>
              <Description>Session or region(= list of sessions) allowed</Description>
              <NeededProperty>Session;Region</NeededProperty>
            </ValueDefinition>
          </Items>
        </ValueDefinition>

          <Category>Reward</Category>
          <NeededProperty>Text</NeededProperty>

        <ValueDefinition>
          <DataType>Choice</DataType>
          <Name>QuestDifficulty</Name>
          <Description>This is the balanced difficulty of this quest</Description>
          <DataSet>QuestDifficulty</DataSet>
        </ValueDefinition>

          <DataType>Boolean</DataType>
          <Name>KeepCheckingPreconditionsWhenRunning</Name>
          <Description>If true, the quest keeps checking the preconditions and will abort automatically if they are not met any longer</Description>
        </ValueDefinition>

Walking.schema:
<Property>
        <Name>Walking</Name>
        <HasImplementation>1</HasImplementation>
        <HasGameTick>1</HasGameTick>
        <IsGameProperty>1</IsGameProperty>
        <ValueDefinition>
          <DataType>Flags</DataType>
          <Name>SpecialMovementType</Name>
          <Description>Do we use any special behaviour?</Description>
          <Category>Walking_Expert</Category>
          <DataSet>SpecialMovementType</DataSet>
          <FunctionName>HasWalkingType</FunctionName>
        </ValueDefinition>
        <ValueDefinition>
          <DataType>Choice</DataType>
          <Name>WalkSequence</Name>
          <Category>Walking_Expert</Category>
          <DataSet>SequenceType</DataSet>
        </ValueDefinition>
        <ValueDefinition>
          <DataType>Choice</DataType>
          <Name>IdleSequence2</Name>
          <Category>Walking_Expert</Category>
          <DataSet>SequenceType</DataSet>
        </ValueDefinition>
        <ValueDefinition>
          <DataType>Time</DataType>
          <Name>ShortenSailsAfter</Name>
          <Description>Sails are shortened when ship is idle for this time. 0:00:00 means "never"</Description>
        </ValueDefinition>
        <ValueDefinition>
          <DataType>Float</DataType>
          <Name>StartHeight</Name>
          <Category>Walking_Expert</Category>
          <IsProValue>1</IsProValue>
        </ValueDefinition>
        <ValueDefinition>
          <DataType>Float</DataType>
          <Name>DiscoverRadius</Name>
          <Description>0 = Disable Discover</Description>
        </ValueDefinition>
        <ValueDefinition>
          <DataType>Integer</DataType>
          <Name>ReservationLength</Name>
          <Description>When using GridReservations (avoiding unit cluttering), this determines the size of the reserved rectangle. Length = from back to front.</Description>
          <Min>0</Min>
          <Max>20</Max>
        </ValueDefinition>
        <ValueDefinition>
          <DataType>Integer</DataType>
          <Name>ReservationWidth</Name>
          <Description>When using GridReservations (avoiding unit cluttering), this determines the size of the reserved rectangle. Width = from left to right</Description>
          <Min>0</Min>
          <Max>10</Max>
        </ValueDefinition>
        <ValueDefinition>
          <DataType>Choice</DataType>
          <Name>PathPlannerLayer</Name>
          <Description>Which Path Planner Layer does the unit use?</Description>
          <DataSet>PathPlannerLayer</DataSet>
        </ValueDefinition>
        <ValueDefinition>
          <DataType>Boolean</DataType>
          <Name>ForcePrimitiveMovement</Name>
          <Description>Enforces simple movement where object does not accelerate / obey turn radii / turn while moving. Object just moves-stops-turns-moves-stops-turns...</Description>
          <Category>Walking_Expert</Category>
        </ValueDefinition>
        <ValueDefinition>
          <DataType>Boolean</DataType>
          <Name>ExpensiveDirSmoothing</Name>
          <Description>Should only be used for important vehicles. Better algorithm for setting rotations (not used for first and last second of each way).</Description>
          <Category>Walking_Expert</Category>
        </ValueDefinition>
        <ValueDefinition>
          <DataType>Float</DataType>
          <Name>TurnAroundRadius</Name>
          <Description>How big of a half-circle is added when the unit gets a new Path and tries to turn into new path direction. (0 = no turnAround)</Description>
          <Category>Walking</Category>
          <Min>0</Min>
          <Max>20</Max>
        </ValueDefinition>
        <ValueDefinition>
          <DataType>Float</DataType>
          <Name>Acceleration</Name>
          <Description>Acceleration</Description>
          <Category>Walking</Category>
          <Min>0.125</Min>
          <Max>96</Max>
        </ValueDefinition>
        <ValueDefinition>
          <DataType>Float</DataType>
          <Name>Deceleration</Name>
          <Description>Deceleration</Description>
          <Category>Walking</Category>
          <Min>0.01</Min>
          <Max>100</Max>
        </ValueDefinition>
        <ValueDefinition>
          <DataType>Float</DataType>
          <Name>TurnRadius</Name>
          <Description>When driving a corner, how much should it be rounded? (corner-radius in world-units) </Description>
          <Category>Walking</Category>
          <Min>0.0125</Min>
          <Max>10</Max>
        </ValueDefinition>
        <ValueDefinition>
          <DataType>Float</DataType>
          <Name>TurnSpeed</Name>
          <Description>How quick can we rotate around Y-axis? (degrees per second)</Description>
          <Category>Walking</Category>
          <Min>0.01</Min>
          <Max>1440</Max>
        </ValueDefinition>
        <ValueDefinition>
          <DataType>Float</DataType>
          <Name>TurnSpeedInPlace</Name>
          <Description>How quick can we rotate around Y-axis when we are turning in place? (degrees per second) - only used for ship-movement</Description>
          <Min>0.01</Min>
          <Max>1440</Max>
        </ValueDefinition>
        <ValueDefinition>
          <DataType>Float</DataType>
          <Name>TurnDeceleration</Name>
          <Description>How much will we slow down in order to drive around a corner? 0 = no slow-down, 1 = slow down a lot</Description>
          <Category>Walking</Category>
          <Min>0</Min>
          <Max>1</Max>
        </ValueDefinition>
        <ValueDefinition>
          <DataType>Float</DataType>
          <Name>TurnMovement</Name>
          <Description>Only Affects Hard turns at beginning of a new Command. 0 = Turn in place, then move. 100 = Move, even if you do not look in the right direction yet. [1-99] = While turning, do a bit of movement. This is only triggered for sharp turns at the beginning of a new movement command and will not happen when turn curves are used as they soften out harsh curves. Currently in game, this is the fallback value that is used when the start curve creation fails.</Description>
          <Category>Walking</Category>
          <Max>100</Max>
        </ValueDefinition>
        <ValueDefinition>
          <DataType>Float</DataType>
          <Name>LeaningSpeed</Name>
          <Description>How fast does unit change its leaning when driving curves? Nice Value: 0.3</Description>
          <Min>0.01</Min>
          <Max>1</Max>
        </ValueDefinition>
        <ValueDefinition>
          <DataType>Float</DataType>
          <Name>LeaningDamping</Name>
          <Description>How fast does unit turn towards "normal" rotation after a curve? Nice value: 0.13</Description>
          <Min>0.01</Min>
          <Max>1</Max>
        </ValueDefinition>
        <ValueDefinition>
          <DataType>Float</DataType>
          <Name>LeaningMaxAngle</Name>
          <Description>Maximum Leaning Angle (in degrees). Positive Value: Lean Inwards, Negative Value: Lean Outwards. 0 = no Leaning. Nice Value: 27</Description>
          <Min>-90</Min>
          <Max>90</Max>
        </ValueDefinition>
        <ValueDefinition>
          <DataType>Float</DataType>
          <Name>ForwardSpeed</Name>
          <Description>Speed in world-units-per-second</Description>
          <Category>Walking_Speed</Category>
          <Min>0.05</Min>
          <Max>40</Max>
        </ValueDefinition>
        <ValueDefinition>
          <DataType>Float</DataType>
          <Name>WindMinSlowdownFactor</Name>
          <Description>When driving against wind, whats the lowest possible Factor on speed</Description>
          <Category>Walking_Speed</Category>
          <Min>0.01</Min>
          <Max>1</Max>
        </ValueDefinition>
        <ValueDefinition>
          <DataType>Float</DataType>
          <Name>WindSlowdownEffectOnTurningSpeed</Name>
          <Description>[0.1 - 1] How much does "WindMinSlowDownFactor" affect us during turns?</Description>
          <Category>Walking_Speed</Category>
          <Min>0.1</Min>
          <Max>1</Max>
        </ValueDefinition>
        <ValueDefinition>
          <DataType>Float</DataType>
          <Name>WindMaxSpeedupFactor</Name>
          <Description>When driving towards wind, whats the max possible Factor on speed</Description>
          <Category>Walking_Speed</Category>
          <Min>1</Min>
          <Max>10</Max>
        </ValueDefinition>
        <ValueDefinition>
          <DataType>Float</DataType>
          <Name>WindSpeedupEffectOnTurningSpeed</Name>
          <Description>[0.1 - 1] How much does "WindMaxSpeedUpFactor" affect us during turns?</Description>
          <Category>Walking_Speed</Category>
          <Min>0.1</Min>
          <Max>1</Max>
        </ValueDefinition>
        <ValueDefinition>
          <DataType>Float</DataType>
          <Name>CargoThreshold</Name>
          <Description>At what cargo-slot fillage percentage (relative) will the CargoWeightStartFactor kick in to alter speed?</Description>
          <Category>Walking_Speed</Category>
          <Min>0</Min>
          <Max>1</Max>
        </ValueDefinition>
        <ValueDefinition>
          <DataType>Float</DataType>
          <Name>CargoStartFactor</Name>
          <Description>When we have cargo-slot-fillage percentage equal to CargoThreshold, what factor do we apply to speed?</Description>
          <Category>Walking_Speed</Category>
          <Min>0.1</Min>
          <Max>1</Max>
        </ValueDefinition>
        <ValueDefinition>
          <DataType>Float</DataType>
          <Name>CargoFullFactor</Name>
          <Description>When we have 100% cargo-slot-fillage percentage, what factor do we apply to speed?</Description>
          <Category>Walking_Speed</Category>
          <Min>0.1</Min>
          <Max>1</Max>
        </ValueDefinition>
        <ValueDefinition>
          <DataType>Float</DataType>
          <Name>DamageThreshold</Name>
          <Description>At how much damage (relative) will the DamageStartFactor kick in to alter speed?</Description>
          <Category>Walking_Speed</Category>
          <Min>0</Min>
          <Max>1</Max>
        </ValueDefinition>
        <ValueDefinition>
          <DataType>Float</DataType>
          <Name>DamageStartFactor</Name>
          <Description>When we have damage equal to DamageThreshold, what factor do we apply to speed?</Description>
          <Category>Walking_Speed</Category>
          <Min>0.1</Min>
          <Max>1</Max>
        </ValueDefinition>
        <ValueDefinition>
          <DataType>Float</DataType>
          <Name>DamageFullFactor</Name>
          <Description>When we have 100% damage, what factor do we apply to speed?</Description>
          <Category>Walking_Speed</Category>
          <Min>0.1</Min>
          <Max>1</Max>
        </ValueDefinition>
        <ValueDefinition>
          <DataType>Float</DataType>
          <Name>MinSlowdownFactor</Name>
          <Description>After applying all speed factors, what minimum-speed-factor do we clamp it to?</Description>
          <Category>Walking_Speed</Category>
          <Min>0.01</Min>
          <Max>1</Max>
        </ValueDefinition>
        <ValueDefinition>
          <DataType>Float</DataType>
          <Name>SessionTransferSpeedFactor</Name>
          <Description>Factor for the speed on the worldmap. A Factor of e.g. 2 means this ship will be transfered from one session to another twice as fast as other ships</Description>
          <Category>Walking_Speed</Category>
        </ValueDefinition>
        <ValueDefinition>
          <DataType>Boolean</DataType>
          <Name>DisableSmoothing</Name>
          <Category>Walking_Expert</Category>
        </ValueDefinition>
        <ValueDefinition>
          <DataType>Float</DataType>
          <Name>IgnoreWeightFactor</Name>
          <Description>Base Value for Upgrades that reduce the effect of weight on the ship speed</Description>
          <Browsable>0</Browsable>
        </ValueDefinition>
        <ValueDefinition>
          <DataType>Float</DataType>
          <Name>IgnoreDamageFactor</Name>
          <Description>Base Value for Upgrades that reduce the effect of damage on the ship speed</Description>
          <Browsable>0</Browsable>
        </ValueDefinition>
        <ValueDefinition>
          <DataType>Boolean</DataType>
          <Name>CreatePathPlannerUnit</Name>
        </ValueDefinition>
        <ValueDefinition>
          <DataType>Choice</DataType>
          <Name>CurveSegmentDensity</Name>
          <Description>When partitioning the Circle into linear segments, how dense should these be?</Description>
          <Category>Walking_Expert</Category>
          <DataSet>CurveSegmentDensity</DataSet>
        </ValueDefinition>
        <ValueDefinition>
          <DataType>Integer</DataType>
          <Name>ShipDoubleClickSelectionRange</Name>
          <Description>double clicking on a ship selects all the ships with the same GUID in this range</Description>
          <Category>Walking_Expert</Category>
        </ValueDefinition>
      </Property>

        <Item>
          <Name>Near</Name>
          <Description>Defines the min and max distance for spawn area calculated from the map borders (playable area). Values are percentages according to the current map's width (if the map's width != map's length, then the longest value is taken as reference)</Description>
          <Id>0</Id>
        </Item>
        <Item>
          <Name>Mid</Name>
          <Description>Defines the min and max distance for spawn area calculated from the map borders (playable area). Values are percentages according to the current map's width (if the map's width != map's length, then the longest value is taken as reference)</Description>
          <Id>1</Id>
        </Item>
        <Item>
          <Name>Far</Name>
          <Description>Defines the min and max distance for spawn area calculated from the map borders (playable area). Values are percentages according to the current map's width (if the map's width != map's length, then the longest value is taken as reference)</Description>
